title: State v. Brown
description: Whether Mr. Brown had a reasonable expectation of privacy in his conversation with his mother in a police interview room, thereby making the police recording of that conversation a violation of his Fourth Amendment and state constitutional rights.
plaintiff_argument: The state argued Mr. Brown did not have a reasonable expectation of privacy in the police station interview room, and therefore the recording was permissible.
defendant_argument: Mr. Brown argued he had a reasonable expectation of privacy in his conversation with his mother, and the recording violated his constitutional rights.
decision_outcome: The court affirmed the Superior Court's order to suppress the recorded conversation between Mr. Brown and his mother, finding that the police violated Mr. Brown's Fourth Amendment and state constitutional rights.

title: Benson v. McKee
description: Whether the Rhode Island General Assembly had the constitutional authority to enact the Reproductive Privacy Act (RPA) and whether the plaintiffs had standing to challenge its enactment.
plaintiff_argument: The plaintiffs argued that the trial justice erred by dismissing their claims for lack of standing, that the General Assembly lacked constitutional authority to enact the RPA, and that their voting rights were suppressed.
defendant_argument: The defendants argued that the plaintiffs lacked standing to bring their claims and that the General Assembly had the constitutional authority to enact the RPA.
decision_outcome: The Supreme Court affirmed the Superior Court's judgment, ruling that the plaintiffs lacked standing to challenge the Reproductive Privacy Act.

title: Zab v. Rhode Island Department of Corrections
description: Whether Rhode Island's civil death statute, which deems life-sentenced prisoners civilly dead and bars them from civil actions, is unconstitutional because it violates their right to access the courts.
plaintiff_argument: The civil death statute is unconstitutional as it violates their fundamental right to access the courts and seek remedies for wrongs, as guaranteed by Article 1, Section 5 of the Rhode Island Constitution.
defendant_argument: The civil death statute is constitutional, does not infringe on the right to access courts, and serves as a legitimate additional sanction for serious criminals, furthering punishment and deterrence.
decision_outcome: The court declared the entirety of Rhode Island's civil death statute (§ 13-6-1) unconstitutional, reversing the lower court's judgments that barred plaintiffs' negligence claims, but affirmed the dismissal of Zab's federal § 1983 claim.

title: Doe v. Brown University
description: Whether the Superior Court erred in dismissing the plaintiff's claims under the Rhode Island Civil Rights Act (RICRA) and Article 1, Section 2 of the Rhode Island Constitution, and whether defendants interfered with her contract with Providence College.
plaintiff_argument: The plaintiff argued that her claims under RICRA were not precluded by a prior federal Title IX dismissal, that Article 1, Section 2 of the Rhode Island Constitution grants a private right of action, and that defendants intentionally interfered with her educational contract.
defendant_argument: The defendants argued that RICRA does not provide a broader cause of action than Title IX, that issue preclusion bars the RICRA claims, that the Rhode Island Constitution does not create a private right of action, and that their actions were not intentional interference with contract.
decision_outcome: The Supreme Court affirmed the judgment of the Superior Court, dismissing all of the plaintiff's claims.
